_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); hotel signals

pit_profile.why: Marriott: 'Consistent with our focus on management, franchising, and licensing, we own very few of our lodging properties'; 'We are a worldwide operator, franchisor, and licensor of hotel, residential, and timeshare properties in 130 countries and territories under 30 brand names'; 'Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully with other hotel properties and home and apartment sharing services for guests'; 'Economic downturns could impact our financial results and growth'; 'An increase in the use of third-party Internet services to book online hotel reservations could adversely impact our business'; 'Our 2018 full-year results reflected a year-over-year increase in the number of properties in our system, favorable demand for our brands in many markets around the world, and generally favorable economic conditions'; and 'On November 30, 2018, we announced a data security incident involving unauthorized access to the Starwood reservations database (the “Data Security Incident”)' ... 'The Data Security Incident could have numerous adverse effects on our business' (its own FY2018 10-K): a hotel management and franchise system whose fees follow the revenues and profits of its hotels through the economy, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it

classification.quality_note: Marriott: 'Consistent with our focus on management, franchising, and licensing, we own very few of our lodging properties'; 'We are a worldwide operator, franchisor, and licensor of hotel, residential, and timeshare properties in 130 countries and territories under 30 brand names'; 'Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully with other hotel properties and home and apartment sharing services for guests'; 'Economic downturns could impact our financial results and growth'; 'An increase in the use of third-party Internet services to book online hotel reservations could adversely impact our business'; 'Our 2018 full-year results reflected a year-over-year increase in the number of properties in our system, favorable demand for our brands in many markets around the world, and generally favorable economic conditions'; and 'On November 30, 2018, we announced a data security incident involving unauthorized access to the Starwood reservations database (the “Data Security Incident”)' ... 'The Data Security Incident could have numerous adverse effects on our business' (its own FY2018 10-K): a hotel management and franchise system whose fees follow the revenues and profits of its hotels through the economy, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.76x; +35% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.23; conservative 2yr +4%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -13.3%/yr (worst year FY09-FY18, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +6.1%/yr (Q4 fee guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +21.5%/yr (FY09-FY18 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +40.4%/yr (best 2-yr run FY09-FY18); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: MAR (retrospective, 2019-12-31) ◎ ACCUMULATE — Ratio B 0.76x (39.9% downside to Bear $91 / +52.5% upside to Bull $231) | Adj composite 2.20 vs market 2.43: gap -0.23 [MODESTLY OVERVALUED] | +35% above the EPP floor $112 (19x FY19E $5.88) | Conservative 2-yr case: +3.6% total (+1.8%/yr) | At 25.7x FY19E the 15% hurdle price $200 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; North American RevPAR +1.0% in Q3 2019, forward fee revenue +5-7% (Q4 2019 fee revenue guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
